2607.17586.title: Detection, Attribution, Narration: An End-to-End Pipeline for Explainable Money Mule Identification
2607.17586.paper_summary: Money mule accounts are critical facilitators of financial fraud, yet detecting them at scale remains challenging due to the heterogeneous nature of transactional and behavioural data. We present an end-to-end pipeline for customer-level mule detection comprising three stages: (1) a LightGBM classifier trained on 280 engineered features spanning transaction patterns, account demographics, network topology, and temporal behaviour; (2) a TreeSHAP attribution layer that decomposes each prediction into feature contributions; and (3) a large language model (LLM) module that converts SHAP attributions into analyst-facing natural-language narratives. We evaluate across three open-weight LLM families and assess explanation quality through analyst feedback. In a live production deployment, the system achieves a yield rate of 89%, up from 61% under the incumbent rule-based system, with monthly alert volume expanding from 211 to 302, reflecting broader true-positive coverage rather than increased noise. This corresponds to a 60% incremental adverse detection beyond existing review workflows, substantially outperforming the rule-based approach. Qualitative feedback from analysts indicates that LLM-generated narratives reduce cognitive load during alert triage. We further discuss implications of deploying LLM-augmented explainability in regulated financial environments.
2607.17586.paper_summary_zh: 金錢騙子帳戶是金融詐騙的重要促進者，但由於交易和行為數據的異質性，在大規模檢測它們仍然具有挑戰性。我們提出了一個端到端的客戶級騙子檢測管道，包含三個階段：(1) 一個基於280個工程特徵的LightGBM分類器，這些特徵涵蓋了交易模式、帳戶人口統計、網絡拓撲和時間行為；(2) 一個TreeSHAP歸因層，將每個預測分解為特徵貢獻；(3) 一個大型語言模型（LLM）模塊，將SHAP歸因轉換為面向分析師的自然語言敘述。我們在三個開放權重的LLM家族中進行評估，並通過分析師反饋評估解釋質量。在實時生產部署中，該系統的產出率達到89%，相比於現有的基於規則的系統的61%有所提升，每月警報量從211擴增至302，這反映了更廣泛的真陽性覆蓋，而不是噪音的增加。這相當於在現有審查工作流程之外的60%增量不利檢測，顯著優於基於規則的方法。分析師的定性反饋表明，LLM生成的敘述在警報篩選過程中減少了認知負擔。我們進一步討論在受監管的金融環境中部署LLM增強解釋能力的影響。
